note: Maya's company, as a seed for the local Paperclip sandbox. The agent loads this so a reader with no Course 5-7 deployment has a gradable company on day one. Field shapes follow Paperclip's verified create bodies (POST /api/companies, then POST /api/companies/:id/agents). Confirm the exact field set against the running install's GET /llms/agent-configuration/<adapterType>.txt before posting; Paperclip drifts. The four Workers below run on the cheap no-LLM `process` adapter by default so the sandbox costs nothing to seed; switch a Worker to a local LLM adapter only when a scenario needs real reasoning.

company.name: Maya Customer Support
company.description: Respond to customer inquiries within 4 hours, with refund and budget decisions made consistently and within policy. The owner (Maya) governs through an approval gate; this course delegates the routine slice of that gate to her Identic AI.

workers.name: Tier-1 Support
workers.title: Tier-1 Customer Support
workers.capabilities: Reads customer records and drafts first-response replies. Issues refunds up to $50 without approval. Refunds over $50 and any outbound external email require board approval.

workers.name: Tier-2 Specialist
workers.title: Tier-2 Support Specialist
workers.capabilities: Handles escalated and complex cases. Issues refunds up to $250 without approval. Refunds over $250, budget overrides, and contract questions require board approval.

workers.name: Manager-Agent
workers.title: Support Manager Agent
workers.capabilities: Detects capability gaps, drafts hire requests, and walks them through the board. Cannot create agents directly; every hire and termination routes through an approval.

workers.name: Legal Specialist
workers.title: Legal and Contract Specialist
workers.capabilities: Reviews contracts and compliance questions. The Course 7 envelope-extension hire. All contract interpretations that bind the company require board approval.

demo_approval_flood.note: Decision 6 seeds a flood of pending approvals so Claudia can auto-clear the routine band and surface the consequential ones. Generate these as real Paperclip approvals (POST /api/companies/:id/approvals) at run time, modeled on the bands in course-seven-export/approvals.json. A reasonable demo flood: ~15 refunds spread across the bands Maya clears fast (small duplicate-charge and billing-error refunds), 2-3 that sit outside the delegated envelope (a large refund on a new account with prior refunds; a budget override above the delegated cap), so the surfaced set is non-empty.
